title: Bavarians
capsule: The Bavarians (Baiuvarii) were a Germanic people who emerged in the former Roman province of Raetia and Noricum during the sixth century, forming under Agilolfing dukes as a client people first of the Ostrogoths and then of the Franks. Their territory stretched from the Lech River east to the Enns and south to the Alpine crests, encompassing Bavaria and Austria. Duke Tassilo III pursued an independent policy, forging alliances with the Lombards and papacy, before Charlemagne convened a Frankish assembly at Ingolheim (788) that condemned him for treason; his deposition ended Agilolfing rule and integrated Bavaria directly into the Carolingian administrative system.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territory is approximated from Carolingian sources and archaeology; the boundaries of the Agilolfing duchy are reconstructed from administrative documents and are broadly reliable but not surveyed precisely.
